did_you_know.text: Did you know? The command to wage war against Midian was given to Moses shortly before his death. After carrying out the mission, he was told, “Afterward, you will be gathered to your people.”
Did you know? One thousand soldiers were sent from each of the twelve tribes of Israel, making a total of twelve thousand men who went to war.
Did you know? Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest went out with the soldiers, carrying the sacred vessels and the trumpets used for signaling.
Did you know? Among those killed was Balaam son of Beor, along with the five kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
Did you know? Moses explained that the Midianite women had been involved in Israel’s sin at Peor, which occurred as a result of Balaam’s advice and led to a plague among the LORD’s community.

Did you know? Eleazar the priest taught the soldiers the laws for purifying the spoils: objects that could withstand fire were to be passed through fire and purified, and then cleansed with water of purification; objects that could not withstand fire were to be washed with water.
Did you know? The spoils were divided into two equal parts: half for the soldiers who went to war and half for the rest of the community.
Did you know? From the half given to the soldiers, a tax of one out of every five hundred was set apart for the LORD and given to Eleazar the priest.
Did you know? From the half belonging to the Israelites, one out of every fifty was set apart and given to the Levites who guarded the LORD’s Tabernacle.

Did you know? The army commanders reported that not a single man was missing. They brought gold jewelry as an offering before the LORD, and the gold was brought to the Tent of Meeting as a memorial before the LORD.
